data.title: bn-2og: M0.6.2 Run the contract fixtures through Investigation's shipped public interface

data.body: P1: The frozen-record gate does not bind the behavior that produced 12/12. It checks only case names and three token substrings, so semantic drift can leave the record claiming qualification while all static checks pass. I demonstrated a valid adapter string that forces strict_artifact_inventory false, replaces decoded binary bytes with b'', and removes validate_as after assigning strict_json; validate_record still succeeds because every token remains. Bind the conformance record to SHA-256 digests of at least run.py and investigation.py (and validate those digests), then add negative mutations proving any fixture/adapter byte drift invalidates the frozen result. Without that, the new static drift gate can falsely attest the exact properties M0.6 is meant to qualify.

P1: The checker also ignores most normative conformance-record fields, so the record can overclaim the qualified slice while the gate stays green. I changed qualified_capabilities to power-loss durability, emptied limits and requalify_on, and replaced both build.argv and execution.argv with unrelated commands; validate_record still passed. Validate the complete frozen build/execution argv, public interface/environment, capability list, limits and requalification triggers (or bind the canonical record), with negative tests for scope/limit/trigger drift. M1.4 must not consume a machine-readable record whose unsupported guarantees are unprotected.

Fixed in 0435a23: the record now carries SHA-256 for run.py, driver.py, and investigation.py; the checker hashes the actual bytes and requires the exact recorded map. Regression mutations preserve the former tokens while disabling strict inventory, discarding binary decoding, removing strict_json before ingest, or remapping invalid_json, and all now fail. Focused 10/10 and full just check pass.

Fixed in 0435a23: validation now requires the complete exact record shape, archive/binary identities, version/interface/commit, build and execution argv/toolchain/env, protocol/case/result scope, supported and unsupported capabilities, limits, triggers, and execution-input digests. Negative tests cover power-loss overclaim, empty limits/triggers, unrelated argv, and archive/digest drift. Focused 10/10 and full just check pass.
